Identify the key concept first.
Eliminate obviously wrong options.

questionText: In a 3×3 magic square, the sums of each row, column, and diagonal are:
questionLatex: \text{In a 3×3 magic square, all row/column/diagonal sums are:}
hints: What makes a magic square 'magic'?
The special property is that every row, every column, and both diagonals add up to the SAME number.
This same number is called the 'magic constant.' It's equal in all directions!

stepByStep.text: A magic square has a special property: all rows, columns, and diagonals have the same sum.
This sum is called the magic constant. It's EQUAL in all directions.

misconceptions.B: If sums were different, it wouldn't be a magic square!
misconceptions.C: 9 is the count of cells in a 3×3 square, not the sum
misconceptions.D: 15 is the magic constant only when using numbers 1-9. Other sets give different constants.

questionText: In a 3×3 magic square, the magic constant (sum of each row) equals:
hints: There's a special relationship between the magic constant and the centre number.
Look at any magic square: if the centre is 5, the magic constant is 15. If centre is 8, constant is 24.
The pattern: magic constant = 3 × centre number

stepByStep.text: In a 3×3 magic square, the magic constant = 3 × centre number.
Answer: 3 times the central box number.

misconceptions.A: This is not a magic square property
misconceptions.C: Adding 9 doesn't follow any magic square rule
misconceptions.D: 9 × centre = sum of ALL 9 numbers, not the magic constant of one row

questionText: In a 3×3 magic square, the sum of ALL nine numbers equals:
hints: There are 3 rows. Each row sums to the magic constant. So total = 3 × magic constant.
Magic constant = 3 × centre. So total = 3 × (3 × centre) = 9 × centre.
Sum of all 9 numbers = 9 × central box number.

stepByStep.text: Total = 3 rows × magic constant per row
Magic constant = 3 × centre. So total = 3 × 3 × centre = 9 × centre.
Sum of all 9 numbers = 9 × central box number.

misconceptions.A: This doesn't match any magic square property
misconceptions.B: This is the magic constant (one row's sum), not the total
misconceptions.C: Squaring the centre doesn't give the total

questionText:
A magic square has 4, ?, 8 in the top row and 5 in the centre.

|  4  |  ?  |  8  |
|  ?  |  5  |  ?  |
|  ?  |  ?  |  ?  |

When completed, which of these numbers will NOT be used?
hints: Centre = 5. Magic constant = 3 × 5 = 15.
Row 1: 4 + ? + 8 = 15, so ? = 3. This uses numbers from a set around 5.
Sum of all 9 numbers = 9 × 5 = 45. The standard 1-9 magic square uses numbers 1 through 9. Number 11 is outside this range!

stepByStep.text: Sum of all 9 = 9 × 5 = 45. Numbers 1-9 sum to 45 ✓.
The magic square uses numbers 1 through 9. 11 is NOT in this range.

misconceptions.C: 9 IS used in the standard 1-9 magic square
misconceptions.D: 6 IS used in the standard 1-9 magic square

questionText: Nine consecutive natural numbers from 3 to 11 are used to form a magic square. Which number will be placed in the central box?
questionLatex: \text{Numbers 3 to 11 in a magic square. Centre} = ?
hints: For 9 consecutive numbers, the centre of a magic square is always the middle number.
Numbers 3 to 11: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11. The middle (5th) number is 7.
Also verify: sum = 9 × 7 = 63. Constant = 63/3 = 21. Row check: any row sums to 21 ✓

stepByStep.text: For consecutive numbers, the centre of the magic square is always the middle number.

misconceptions.A: 11 is the largest number, not the centre
misconceptions.B: 3 is the smallest number, not the centre

questionText: A 3×3 magic square has 8 in the centre. What is the magic constant?

stepByStep.text: Use the formula: magic constant = 3 × centre

misconceptions.C: Calculated 9 × 8 = 72 (that's the total of ALL numbers, not the row sum)

misconceptions.A: 15 is the total of all 9 numbers (in thirds: 45/3 = 15), not the centre
misconceptions.B: 5 is the magic constant, not the centre value
misconceptions.C: 6/3 = 2, which is the top-left corner, not the centre

questionText:
In this array, each row, column, and diagonal has equal sum. Find X + Y + Z.

|  Z  |    |  4  |
|     |  Y | 15 |
|  X  |    |  8  |
hints: The diagonal from top-right to bottom-left is: 4, Y, X. The other diagonal is: Z, Y, 8.
Y is the centre. Magic constant = 3 × Y. Also look at column 3: 4 + 15 + 8 = 27. So constant = 27.
Y = 27/3 = 9. Diagonal: Z + 9 + 8 = 27, so Z = 10. Other diagonal: 4 + 9 + X = 27, so X = 14. X+Y+Z = 14+9+10 = 33.

misconceptions.B: Likely made a small arithmetic error in one of the calculations
misconceptions.C: Likely miscounted which diagonal to use
misconceptions.D: The answer is 33, which IS one of the options

questionText: In a cross pattern, 5 is in the centre. The numbers 1, 3, 7, 9 are placed at the four ends so that both lines through the centre have the same sum. Which number is opposite to 1?
questionLatex: \text{Centre = 5. Ends: 1, 3, 7, 9. Same sum through centre. Opposite to 1?}
hints: If a number is at one end, the other end of the same line plus the centre must equal the same sum for both lines.
Total of all 5 numbers = 1+3+5+7+9 = 25. Two lines share the centre. Each line: end + 5 + end = sum. Both sums equal.
Sum of each line = (25 + 5) ÷ 2 = 15. Line with 1: 1 + 5 + ? = 15. So ? = 9.

misconceptions.A: 5 is the centre, not an end

questionText: A magic square has this first row: 6, 15, 3. What is the magic constant and the centre number?
hints: Magic constant = sum of any row. Row 1: 6 + 15 + 3 = ?
Constant = 24. Centre = constant ÷ 3.
Centre = 24 ÷ 3 = 8

misconceptions.B: Centre is not equal to the constant
misconceptions.D: Centre is not half the constant — it's one-third!

questionText: A, B, and C are three numbers. A + B = 10, B + C = 15, A + C = 11. What is the value of A + B + C?

misconceptions.A: Used 2(A+B+C) = 36 but forgot to divide by 2
misconceptions.D: Just used the largest equation value
